Skydive is designed to actually help you grow your business by autonomously taking action throughout your company.

results.title: Anything Launches Skydive Platform for Employees to ...
results.content:
Anything, the AI app builder used by more than 1 million people, has launched Skydive publicly following a closed beta involving more than 20 companies. The platform gives each agent its own cloud computing environment with access to a browser, file system and terminal, allowing agents to work across tools including Slack, email, iMessage, desktop applications and the web.

The idea is to move agents beyond question-and-answer interfaces and narrowly defined automations. Skydive agents can be assigned roles, given access to approved tools and taught how a company handles particular processes, with the goal of carrying tasks from request through completion. [...] Skydive addresses some of those concerns by handling model access, computing sandboxes, permissions, security and underlying infrastructure. Administrators can centrally manage access, data, AI usage and spending while employees build agents within those controls.

The platform supports more than 170 frontier and open-weight AI models. Each agent operates from its own cloud computer, meaning tasks can continue running when an employee’s personal computer is offline.

results.title: Anything Launches Skydive, a Platform for Building AI Coworkers
results.content:
Skydive agents aren't chatbots or workflows. They're coworkers. Each has a name, a role, and its own cloud computer, so they can use all tools a team uses, a browser, a file system, and a terminal. They work across Slack, email, iMessage, desktop, and the web, learning how a team operates and carrying work from request to completion, even when their laptops are closed.

Anything built Skydive to run its own company. Its 15-person team now works alongside more than 150 agents across customer support, engineering, marketing, growth, sales, operations, and the office itself.

Now, any company can build the coworkers they're missing.

Built for the work companies never get to [...] The person closest to the work can now build the agent.

A support leader can create an engineering lead who fixes every support request. A growth lead can create an outbound team. An operations manager can create a coworker for the repetitive job that stole their focus from what's most important.

Teams can begin with templates for roles such as chief of staff, customer support, SEO, or bug investigation, then teach each agent how their company actually works. Agents improve as they learn the team's tools, preferences, and processes. [...] "Our mission has always been to make it extremely easy for regular people to build," said Dhruv Amin, co-founder of Anything. "Apps were the first version of that. Agents are next. Inside Anything, they haven't replaced a single hire. They've taken on jobs we never had the headcount for and given every person here leverage that used to require an entire team."

From idea to agent without reinventing infra

Each agent runs on its own cloud computer with a browser, file system, and terminal. Skydive handles model access, sandboxes, permissions, security, and infrastructure, so teams can focus on defining the job rather than assembling the system underneath it.
